audit.whatIsWrong: Eight strings across both layers call the root 'RQ root-and-tether' (spikes[0], spikes[2], early, mid, late, whys[1], whys[2], whys[5], wants.foe[1]). The root is attributed to Mantra-Q throughout.
audit.why: Karma's root is Focused Resolve (W) — 'Karma creates a tether between herself and a targeted enemy... If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted.' Mantra on W 'strengthens the link, healing herself and extending the root duration'. Mantra on Q creates a damage cataclysm and roots nothing. So the ability to track is RW, not RQ. A Mel player watching Karma's Q for a root will step into the actual one, and will dodge the wrong spell all lane. This is the same class of error as the calibration examples given for Brand and Cassiopeia.
audit.corrected: The root is Focused Resolve (W), a targeted tether; Mantra-W extends it. Mantra-Q is a delayed damage zone with no CC.

audit.whatIsWrong: `early`, `whys[0]` and `wants.foe[0]` all say Karma's Q out-ranges Radiant Volley.
audit.why: Inner Flame is 950. Radiant Volley is 950. They are identical, so there is no range deficit to play around and the whole 'don't throw Q if she's holding hers' premise is false — this is a symmetric poke trade Mel can take.
audit.corrected: Both Qs are 950. Neither champion out-ranges the other with Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: `whys[1]` says her root 'out-ranges Solar Snare, winning the first committed trade'.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is 675 range. Solar Snare is 1000. Mel out-ranges the tether by 325 units — the exact inverse of what the text claims. Worse, this hides Mel's actual answer: the tether breaks on distance, and Rebuttal grants movement speed, so W-into-walk-out is a hard counter to a landed Focused Resolve.
audit.corrected: Solar Snare (1000) comfortably out-ranges Focused Resolve (675). If the tether does land, break it — Rebuttal's move speed is the tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[0]` and `whys[1]` place the empowered-root threat at level 2-3.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit: 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point.' Karma can empower from the moment the game starts. The threat window opens at level 1 with a W point, not at 2-3.
audit.corrected: Mantra is live at level 1; the RW root exists as soon as she takes a W point.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears in either layer; full `breakdown.cooldowns` says 'break it with range or line of sight' with no timing.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is a flat 12s at every rank — it never gets shorter, so the punish window is a fixed, countable 12s all game. Inner Flame is 9/8/7/6/5s. Mantra is 40/38/36/34s and is pulled down by Gathering Fire whenever her damaging abilities hit, so chip on the wave is what accelerates her next empowered cast.
audit.corrected: Focused Resolve is a flat 12s; Mantra is 40s at rank 1 but Gathering Fire shortens it every time she lands damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Grievous Wounds despite `wants.foe[2]` and `mid` complaining that she out-sustains the short trades.
audit.why: Mantra-W heals Karma as it extends the root, which is the sustain the entry is describing. Anti-heal timing is what makes Mel's chip stick into a long lane.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal answers the Mantra-W self-heal, not the E shield.

audit.why: 48.57% over 35 games — the largest sample in this slice — carried consistently, and it matches the EVEN 5.5/10 grade. No elo-tier language present.

notes: The packet flags 'Golden Eclipse's' in `late` as a probable wrong ability name (distance 2). It is a false positive — Golden Eclipse is correct per champ-data/_kits/mel.json and the string is a possessive. No edit made on that basis. Separately, `wants.you[2]` claims Rebuttal reflects her poke back 'as my own magic damage'; Inner Flame is a projectile so the reflect itself is sound, but I found nothing in the kit files establishing what damage type a reflected projectile deals, so I left the damage-type claim alone rather than assert it either way.
